title: Analytic inverse problems with finitely many random measurements
summary: While infinite-dimensional inverse problems are traditionally analyzed assuming continuous data, practical applications rely on finitely many discrete measurements. Recent deterministic approaches establish that unknowns belonging to a $d$-dimensional model class can be stably recovered from finitely many measurements. However, for severely ill-posed problems, such as the Calderón problem and inverse scattering, the known constructions may require a number of measurements that is exponential in $d$.
